# portholeView

Decides what the status spot shows, as a pure function of the service's snapshot, its last heartbeat and this clock, so a window, a CLI and a test reach the same answer.

```tsx
import { portholeView } from "@/registry/ouro/lib/ouro/porthole-view";
```

## Example

```tsx
const view = portholeView(source.getSnapshot(), source.lastBeatAt(), Date.now());
view.text; // "Updated just now"
```

## Usage

One item at a time: the most urgent (`action`, then `error`, `working`, `rest`); on a tie, the newest `since`. At rest it says "Updated just now" only while every area was verified within `freshWithinMs` (the area's own, for one the service reads on an interval) and none has been in trouble for `troubleAfterMs`; otherwise the real age of the area verified longest ago ("Updated 4 min ago"). A `rest` item, such as "Up to date", shows over "Updated just now" only: past fresh, or unknown, the age line or "Status unknown" wins and the item waits in the open spot's lines. It says "Status unknown" when an area has never been verified, when the snapshot has no areas or another version, or when the heartbeat is older than `heartbeatTimeoutMs` or too far ahead of this clock to check. A stopped heartbeat outranks every item, an `action` too: nothing the service said can be trusted as live, and the action's button would reach a service that cannot answer, so the item waits in the open spot's lines. `nextChangeAt` is the one moment to look again.

## Use instead when

- Use `portholeStatus` instead for the JSON an agent or a CLI reads, and the `Porthole` component to show it.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `snapshot` | `PortholeSnapshot` |  |
| `heartbeatAt` | `number` |  |
| `now` | `number` |  |
| `options` | `PortholeViewOptions` | `{}` |

## Returns

`PortholeView`
